questions.q: Which sugar is the C4 epimer of D-glucose?
questions.explain: D-Glucose (C2–C5: R, L, R, R) and D-galactose (R, L, L, R) differ only at C4. Mannose is the C2 epimer, allose the C3 epimer, and fructose is a ketose (a functional isomer).

questions.q: Which pair of sugars are NOT epimers?
questions.explain: D-Mannose and D-galactose differ at both C2 and C4, so they are diastereomers but not epimers; epimers differ at exactly one stereocentre.

questions.q: An open-chain aldohexose has how many stereoisomers in all, and how many of them are D-sugars?
questions.explain: An aldohexose has four stereocentres (C2–C5), giving 2⁴ = 16 stereoisomers, half of which (8) are D.

questions.q: Lengthening D-xylose by one carbon at the CHO end (Kiliani–Fischer synthesis) gives which pair of D-aldohexoses?
questions.explain: The new stereocentre appears at C2, so each parent gives a pair of C2 epimers; the old centres of xylose (R, L, R) become C3–C5, matching D-gulose and D-idose.
